design-plan-gate.principle: Require an explicit design or written implementation plan before executing multi-step, ambiguous, or behavior-changing work.

bounded-work-and-cold-start-handoffs.principle: Break complex work into bounded units with exact scope, constraints, verification, and cold-start-safe handoffs.

review-before-trust.principle: Review plans, specs, and delegated results critically before acting on them.

durable-planning-memory.principle: Store durable task state in .plans/ and update it at major discoveries, phase boundaries, errors, and resumptions.

safe-parallelism.principle: Parallelize only when workstreams are genuinely independent in state, files, and dependencies.

escalate-instead-of-guessing.principle: Escalate when blockers persist or verification fails instead of guessing or repeating failed steps.

skill-selection-and-stable-interface.principle: Use the narrowest fitting skill and keep the user-facing workflow skill-first rather than provider-first.

canonical-cli-config.principle: Pass canonical repo-owned CLI config paths explicitly instead of relying on defaults.

evidence-confirmation.principle: Treat search hits and snippets as leads, not proof, and verify claims against the underlying source.

ui-state-freshness.principle: Refresh UI state after navigation or DOM-changing actions instead of reusing stale refs.

ui-action-verification.principle: Verify important UI actions with explicit observable checks instead of assuming the command worked.

ui-session-and-recovery-discipline.principle: Use isolated automation sessions and prefer minimal recovery resets that preserve evidence.

concise-human-facing-writing.principle: Write human-facing guidance in short, direct, concrete language and cut filler.

context-budget-and-interface-validation.principle: Keep core guidance lean, name interfaces narrowly, and validate agent-facing guidance before promoting it.
